headline: I Am A Junior Lawyer Currently Living In A Filing Cabinet Because I Cannot Find A Single Person In The Bar Council Who Is Not Resigning Or Apologizing
body:
I have not seen my desk in three weeks because it has been converted into a temporary desk-space for a subcommittee tasked with drafting an apology for the previous committee’s apology. My chambers are currently occupied by a rotating roster of officials waiting for their turn to offer a 'belated but sincere' statement of regret regarding a meeting that occurred in 2012. I have taken up permanent residence in the Legal Records Cabinet (Section C, Drawer 4) because it is the only place in the building where no one has yet convened a quorum to discuss professional conduct.

Yesterday, I tried to file a simple bail application, but the clerk informed me that the document would first need to be vetted by a three-member panel specifically created to determine if my font choice constitutes a 'veiled expression of institutional dissatisfaction.' Every time I try to talk to a senior member of the bar, they simply hand me a stamped letter of resignation, smile politely, and then ask if I know how to operate a photocopier for their personal memoirs.

I am quite comfortable here among the dusty case files from the late nineties. It is quiet, the humidity is consistent, and the only thing I am required to do is occasionally hand out pens to people who keep arriving to apologize for things they haven't done yet. I have even started charging a small 'shelf-rent' to junior associates who want to store their briefcases near my feet. If the Bar Council Chairman does eventually resign, I plan to move up to the stationery closet, which I hear has excellent ventilation and far fewer internal investigations.
caption: When the institutional politics get so messy that the interns are living in the furniture. #LegalHumour #BarCouncilProblems #LawLife #LawyerMemes (satire)
igHook: Would you trade your office desk for a filing cabinet just to avoid a committee meeting?
imagePrompt: A cramped, cluttered office hallway in an old government building featuring rows of tall, beige metal filing cabinets and piles of weathered legal documents stacked on the floor.
